newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Nov base money growth slows to 7.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Nov base money growth slows to 7.6 pct.

text.p: The Philippines' base money in November slackened to a year-on-year growth of 7.6 percent from 13.2 percent in the previous month, the Central Bank reported on Monday.
It attributed the slowing down in money supply growth to its open market operations.
The government's budget surplus position also contributed to the slowdown since it minimised withdrawals from deposit balances with the Central Bank, the statement said.
Year-on-year growth of reserve money, a main determinant of base money, likewise slowed to 8.4 percent in November from 13.7 the previous month, the Central Bank said.
It said both base and reserve money were more than 40 billion pesos below programme ceilings based on the latest preliminary data.

M3, the broadest measure of money supply, stood at 799.5 billion pesos in September, more than 40 billion pesos below the indicative ceiling under the economic programme with the International Monetary Fund, it added.
